meta.title: Better Scholar: your author role and venue rank on Google Scholar
meta.description: A free Chrome extension for Google Scholar profiles. It shows your author role and the CCF / CORE rank of the venue on each paper, and counts your papers in one table.
hero.title: Your role and the venue rank on every paper
hero.sub: A free Chrome extension for Google Scholar profiles. It colours each paper by your author role, shows the CCF and CORE rank of its venue, and counts your papers in one table.
hero.note: Free and open source · Chrome, Edge, Brave and other Chromium browsers · 30 languages
shot.caption: A made-up profile with real venues. Each row has the colour of your role, chips show the rank, and the panel on the right counts the papers.
how.title: How it reads a paper
how.note: Two made-up papers at real venues. Each step shows what the extension's own code finds in them.
how.s1.title: Find your name
how.s1.text: It finds the profile's name in the author line. Your place in the line gives your role: first, co-first, second or last author.
how.s2.title: Look up the venue
how.s2.text: It looks for the venue in the CCF and CORE lists, by its full name or by its acronym. A sure match gives a rank chip.
how.s3.title: Never guess
how.s3.text: A workshop, a poster or a Findings paper is not the main conference. A venue that the lists do not hold for certain gets no chip.
how.s4.title: Count
how.s4.text: The panel counts each paper once, by your role and by the rank. Click a number to see its papers.
how.secondary: secondary track: no rank, no chip
features.title: What else it does
f.awards.title: Awards and talks
f.awards.text: Chips for best papers, test-of-time awards and Oral, Spotlight or Highlight talks. They come from the authors' own words and from official award pages.
f.complete.title: Full author lists
f.complete.text: Scholar cuts long author lists with “…”, and this can hide your role. One click reads the full lists from Scholar's paper pages.
f.merge.title: Duplicates merged
f.merge.text: Scholar sometimes lists one paper two times. A switch makes them one entry and adds up their citations.
f.yours.title: Your own layout
f.yours.text: Every part of the panel has its own switch. Choose the colours, the order of the parts and your own names for them.
f.private.title: Private
f.private.text: No account, no analytics, no tracking. All the work happens in your browser, and the rank lists are inside the extension.
f.lang.title: 30 languages
f.lang.text: The extension speaks your language. It can also open Scholar itself in a language that you choose.
demo.title: Try the settings page
demo.hint: This is the real settings page of the extension. Change a setting and the preview changes with it. Point at a part of the preview to hide, move or rename it.
demo.local: Your changes stay in this browser.
demo.frame: Better Scholar settings page, an interactive demo
ops.title: Search with operators
ops.note: Press [/] on a profile to search all its papers. Add operators to your words to filter the list.
ops.cite.title: Citations
ops.cite.text: Papers with more or fewer citations than a number.
ops.tier.title: Rank
ops.tier.text: Papers at venues with a given CCF or CORE rank.
ops.role.title: Role
ops.role.text: Papers where you are the first, co-first, second or last author.
ops.year.title: Year
ops.year.text: Papers from before, after or in a year, or from the last few years.
ops.honors.title: Awards and talks
ops.honors.text: Papers with a best-paper or test-of-time award, or with an Oral, Spotlight or Highlight talk.
ops.reset.title: Clear all
ops.reset.text: One key clears the search, the selected cell and every filter.
export.title: Copy your papers
export.note: One button for each format: for a CV, a grant form, LaTeX or a spreadsheet. Below is the real output for four made-up papers.
numbers.title: By the numbers
numbers.note: The build counts these from the extension's code and data. Numbers that grow with each fix are rounded down.
numbers.venues: ranked venues in the CCF and CORE lists
numbers.names: venue names that Scholar prints but the lists do not have
numbers.guards: checks that stop a wrong rank
numbers.real: real venue lines from Scholar, each result looked at
numbers.tests: unit tests, and an end-to-end suite in a real browser
install.title: Install
install.step1: Download the project from GitHub: click the green Code button, then Download ZIP. Unzip the file.
install.step2: Open chrome://extensions and turn on Developer mode.
install.step3: Click “Load unpacked” and select the src folder. Then open a Google Scholar profile.
install.note: Edge, Brave and other Chromium browsers use the same steps. A Chrome Web Store version may come later.
honest.title: Limits
honest.l1: The ranks come from today's lists. In the year of a paper, its venue may have had a different rank.
honest.l2: CCF says that its list is not a basis for academic evaluation.
honest.l3: It never guesses. A venue that it cannot place gets no chip, and the panel lists it.
